comics.Title: 5 Min Ago Lounge
comics.AuthorNotes: This is my favorite strip of the collection and I am glad it is the first. It really inspired me to tell the stories of my VRChat adventures. The stories of the moments, places, and most importantly, of the people who inhabit them. When I introduce Maximus Comics, I show this one first. Many have told me how they relate to that moment of falling in like for someone in VR and the lifecycle it bears at times. Certainly, as a spectator if not participant. There is a lot of emotion in this strip for me as I have lived this moment myself. Someone once told me, when I first joined VRChat, that people come and go and don't stick around. It would be easy to let the cynicism in me agree, but instead, it fills me with the greatest of hope, for if these moments exist, then so too, do the moments of the love that lasts.

comics.Title: Menu Dimension
comics.AuthorNotes: This strip introduces the first villain of the comics and my greatest arch nemesis of all time: The Menu System. I am afraid to admit the number of times that I have been lost in the menus of VR. Where was that hair toggle at again?!? Which of the 9344 menus contain that avatar nameplate visibility toggle ?!?!

comics.Title: Voice Mod Monastary
comics.AuthorNotes: My favorite part of this is that Brother Reverb, when they speak, has a maximum void mod deep reverb voice that echoes and shakes the stained glass. I also imagine that said person has the squeakiest and highest pitches of voice possible.

comics.Title: Customity Court
comics.AuthorNotes: I have discovered the great world of VRChat Drama Courts. What a chaotic bit of pandemonium it is! With Structure! I always imagine the types of cases people bring up in these role playing worlds. I imagine that all arguments in VRChat should end up with some drama court audience to mull over: even if it comes to two friends arguing if their same base avatars are unique enough to be worn together.

comics.Title: The Rave Peddler
comics.AuthorNotes: This goes out to all those quest users joining the raves of bleeding eyes.

comics.Title: E Girl Rep Exchange
comics.AuthorNotes: The main currency in VRChat is interesting. It isn't necessarily world collections, or avatars, or unique Booth props. Is it Perception? Perceived coolness? Wit? The gift of gab where gab is the primary interface? Technical knowledge perhaps? Nah!! It is the average day traders of VRChat Drama who watch the market like one habituatally wants to know which VR game of thrones character is next to get banned, and by who! The armies of westeros conflict in VR and I am amused at the idea that there is some hard core stock like trading system that is trading off these secrets. Often times, there will be a headpats exports/imports, cuddle futures, and a mutual trust Index. Until it crashes.

comics.Title: Calibration Cathedral
comics.AuthorNotes: The Calibration Cathedral is the faction I chose to represent the Full Body Trackers in VR, with their seemingly cult like revery. They have to be in some church somewhere worshipping the great TPose in a religious manner pursuing the perfect tracking alignment that can only be achieved through divinity.

comics.Title: Velvet Trials
comics.AuthorNotes: Ah yes, B Club! This is the first story arc of the fictional, and classically comic driven style stories I want to pursue. This story arc starts with the introduction of the Velvet Rope Club, whose society is built on User roles and class caste systems, and of course, the blood sport it fostures in gaining those roles.

comics.Title: Collectible
comics.AuthorNotes: Here we introduce The Collector. A villain of maximum materialistic greed. Their sole purpose is to collect every other person's valuable avatars. The more unique the avatar the better.

comics.Title: Most Of You Will Die
comics.AuthorNotes: My ideas of a good villain, especially in movies and shows, is that feeling of how real the perceived danger to the henchmen are. The feeling that henchmen are expendable or about to get offed for saying the wrong word. PitBoss here is the right hand man of The Collector and lets the audience know that failure to succeed is met with death.

comics.Title: Important People Leave Foot Prints
comics.AuthorNotes: To counter balance the villain, we choose the exact opposite in the 'hero' role. Meet Patch. Underdog scavenger; bottom-rank outsider; socially immune to drama and role status. His avatar cannot be copied because it is assembled from hundreds of modified, broken and improvised parts. Patch cannot be tempted with rank because they do not respect it. Cannot be embarrassed by an unfashionable avatar because they built it themselves. They cannot be copied because their avatar is made from hundreds of modified, broken, and improvised components. They cannot be manipulated through drama because they rarely understand that drama is happening. It is also important to establish Patch as a heart of gold, maybe naively so.

comics.Title: Must Collect It
comics.AuthorNotes: Patch shows up on the radars of The Collector during a fishing village scene. I particularly enjoyed adding the idea that the Collector's bodyguards are these overt buff pitbull like furries.

comics.Title: k
comics.AuthorNotes: The society of mole rat people is that collection of 10-15 avatar groups that occupy the corners of every VRChat zone, often with 0.4m tall avatars. They are always crowded in weird places like in cracks, nooks, crannies, and what I amount to as 'mouse holes' in the digital drywall. Since nobody sees these avatars join a world, and they are always there, the lore here is that they use tunnels and caves of hidden exits and arcane knowledge to travel the VR realms. They are often unnoticed and are a fascimile to Tolkien-esque hobbits.

comics.Title: Group Hopping
comics.AuthorNotes: Nothing like a group world hopping session looking for magical places and cosmic adventures of where to hang out, only to end up in an optimized box with a single mirror. This also gives the chance to introduce possible new canonical areas such as the Catfish Aquarium, a zone where people go to get catfished or to discover if they have been catfished; like a dating show where the contestants reveal who is behind the screens.

comics.Title: Preflight Checklist
comics.AuthorNotes: It seems appropriate that the locale chosen for an impromptu at back room VR romance spawns from the 5 minute ago lounge. Not only because of the 5 minute timer... but it also almost seems to be a ritual that for 2 hours, both people go through Full Body Tracking technical problems.

comics.Title: Got to go
comics.AuthorNotes: Sooooo many times have I seen someone say they had to go. For work, care for a baby, do chores, and all other manners involving the physical world, only for them to not go and end up being the last one standing at the end of the night. Perhaps: Still not quite ready to log out!

comics.Title: BRB
comics.AuthorNotes: Mutes. Nobody reall knows what they are saying. I wanted this to occur at the uWu Embassy, the lore vehicle used to drive diplomacy when the egril drama exchanges collapse and require careful mending of the VRChat peace

comics.Title: Imposter AFK
comics.AuthorNotes: I just assume at this point that nobody is ever trully AFK. We can see you moving around FBT!

comics.Title: Gotta Add Em All
comics.AuthorNotes: There is a little Collector in all of us in VRChat. For some: Avatars. For others: Groups and Friend Invites.

comics.Title: Avatar Upload Support Group
comics.AuthorNotes: Some will know this pain all too well.

comics.Title: Flashlight Emporeum
comics.AuthorNotes: I am still in the phase of introducing new places that have their own lore and gimmick. The horror worlds of VRChat tend to have a lot of batteries lying around. I wonder how all these batteries and flashlights get supplied out. A costco like mega box store explains it! Also, the analogy of any horror world in the Maximus universe. Two things for world designers: Dont make me hold the button down to hold the flashlight. Why do batteries only last 20 seconds !??!? Go find the Flashlight of Revealing here in the comic store.

comics.Title: Still Cant See
comics.AuthorNotes: Yep. Flashlights don't really help in some horror worlds. Why even have them!??!

comics.Title: You First
comics.AuthorNotes: At some point, the main jump scare creature everyone has been avoiding in the Horror worlds , must be sitting there sipping on coffee just waiting for its moment in the encounter.

comics.Title: Everything But
comics.AuthorNotes: When you only have two hands per group member, inventory is valuable in the Puzzle/Horror worlds. So much so that there is a very careful coordination effort by the party to carry, swap and take certain items. Eventually, something has to be left behind. You just never know what item will be that important carry with me.

comics.Title: Open Mic
comics.AuthorNotes: No game is immune to the demons of the open mic 'Chip Crunch'

comics.Title: Going Down
comics.AuthorNotes: Is it me or do none of the elevators ever work in these horror worlds ?! The ones that do work generally have your party in different versions of the world all occupying the same space.

comics.Title: Safety Settings
comics.AuthorNotes: The real horror in the horror worlds are often times the fallback avatars themselves.

comics.Title: Wasnt Me
comics.AuthorNotes: Yeah yeah. We get it. Nobody did it. What do people expect in the mystery game worlds? That the killers will offer their evil status' from mere suggestion? Until then, may the McCarthyism be forever in your favor

comics.Title: You Choose
comics.AuthorNotes: One should take a page out of the uWu's Diplomacy when deciding who wants to kick off a world hopping train by just picking a place and dropping the portal. If the will of the group is to go in, they shall! Else, it may devolve into an hour long no you go, no go ahead, your turn to choose fest.

comics.Title: Nice Ears
comics.AuthorNotes: Never compliment the ears if you aren't willing to take a full Avatar tour.

comics.Title: Frozen Listener
comics.AuthorNotes: A good listener or broken FBT?

comics.Title: Afk Succession
comics.AuthorNotes: Many a great battles have been waged over who gets to pick the music when the hosts playlists end.

comics.Title: The Other Queue
comics.AuthorNotes: A watched queue never lets you in

comics.Title: Call In Progress
comics.AuthorNotes: There was one time I was at a B club and someone had a physical world dispute going in the background to the point where the whole club cuddled around the streamer listening. Eventually the cops went barging in. I have seen utter collapses on the egirl drama exchange because someone was on a call or forgot to mute their mic.

comics.Title: Final Goodbye
comics.AuthorNotes: Some nights are a 5 goodybye type of night. Some are simple. Then there are these kind of nights...

comics.Title: Third Wheel
comics.AuthorNotes: If you plan to go on a VRChat date, make sure to set your status to non joinable unless you want a group date.

comics.Title: Date Assessment
comics.AuthorNotes: Some VRChat dates are really no different than physical ones. The life interview process is still the same.

comics.Title: The Avatar Test
comics.AuthorNotes: I changed Bean There Cafe to Bean Here Cafe. A subtle jab at the feeling of 'oh no not again', I've been here before. The language choice of here vrs. there seemed more natural. The Bean Here Cafe is my fascimile and trope of a typical dating world. Unlike the 5 minute ago lounge which has a focus on cheaper and more hedonistic style relationships, the cafe setting feels like a more legitimized attempt at wanting to know the person. I have many fond memories in various cafes. So much so, that I wanted to capture the feeling, emotion, and goofiness of it all in a more romanticized way that the lounge setting wouldn't allow for.

comics.Title: WASD
comics.AuthorNotes: Communication is fascinating. When you have desktop users outside of VR, they can't point or gesture easily. Instead, gyrations of back and forth FPS controllers is what you are left with, and yet, we all somehow understand each other.

comics.Title: Safety Settings Romance
comics.AuthorNotes: This actually happened to me. I still wonder what fallback they saw to inspire such flattery

comics.Title: Height Negotiation
comics.AuthorNotes: The typical thing you would see at an uWu Embassy

comics.Title: Archaelogist
comics.AuthorNotes: Should I talk to them? Should I not? Let me dig through their bio to find things in common. I guess the thing we had in common was corner gooning and people watching.

comics.Title: Just Friends Photoshoot
comics.AuthorNotes: In the realm of falling in like with someone, it is always interesting to imagine how two people taking photos of each other for their profile pictures do so under the 'just friends' photoshoot that must have gone down as the genesis of their profile

comics.Title: Sit-uationship
comics.AuthorNotes: A more literal sense of the word. Often times you can tell who is in what potential relationships just by how others sit next to each other. They aren't fooling anybody!

comics.Title: Typing
comics.AuthorNotes: When you are dating a mute, you do spend a lot of time wondering what the ... will come out to being in. Sometimes they are typing for what amounts to hours of cosmic adventures... Just to find out in the end it was a simple message. Perhaps they were debating between: lol, rofl, haha, :), etc...

comics.Title: Date With UI
comics.AuthorNotes: Not all dates at the Bean Here Cafe start out great! I know it is a lost connection when it is evident they are clearly UI surfing. In this strip it is counterbalanced by the overt ridiculousness and seriousness of the date.

comics.Title: Gooner
comics.AuthorNotes: Gooning and sniffing may be separate things in VRChat, but I do see a strong overlap. Here I imagine is how an innocent VRChatizen comes across their first public gooner encounter. And like all public crowds at popular worlds, they are always lurking in the crowd somewhere waiting to strike.

comics.Title: Private Instance
comics.AuthorNotes: Much like the Sit-uationship and a Just Friends photoshoot, the secretive 'sneaking out' puppy love is always adorable and cute to tease partners who haven't admitted to such a relationship yet when they go 'off into a world' for 5 minutes by themselves.

comics.Title: Adoption
comics.AuthorNotes: Some sub cultures have their own customs and languages. Even in the niche VRChat worlds. I won't pretend to understand them all.

comics.Title: Limited By Imagination
comics.AuthorNotes: Who can really resist a good meme?

comics.Title: So Tired
comics.AuthorNotes: It really is hard to go to bed when you have gotten pulled in, through gravitational forces alone, into one of the black hole cuddle piles.

comics.Title: Liminal
comics.AuthorNotes: Exits within exits. Pools in the water of the ocean from a faucet of a fill bathroom sink! The levels of recursion know no bounds! And each liminal inside a liminal makes time slow down by half.

comics.Title: Accessorize And Goon
comics.AuthorNotes: It is of particular note when you have face tracking, you get caught gooning over others pretty regularly. The fix: Don't be creeps!

comics.Title: Not Every Chair Is Lore
comics.AuthorNotes: The syndrome of the red herring. That is really one of my favorite thrills of these worlds. What is a key object and what is a stray mesh left over in Unity...

comics.Title: Dont Touch Anything
comics.AuthorNotes: I have casual friends, stoner friends, and everyone in between. When stoners and gamers collide it is interesting. The gamers impulse is to speed run everything while my stoner friends want to sit and contemplate the metaphysical beings of a puzzle room. The one rule we generally go by is to not trigger or click anything until everyone is there.

comics.Title: Rabbit Hole
comics.AuthorNotes: When I first joined VRChat, I was new to the netizens of this world that inhabit it. Everyone kind of goes through that phase of learning how deep the internet wells go. It usually starts off with some public avatar, and eventually one comes across the first hint of adult themed content. It usually starts by seeing the no 'ERP' signs everywhere and thus begins them down the rabbit hole: What is ERP?

comics.Title: Backrooms
comics.AuthorNotes: I am not sure if this is a current 2026 trend or not. There are A LOT of back rooms variants. They are on the Switch2, Roblox, you name it. The phenomenon isn't lost here.

comics.Title: Escape Room Commentator
comics.AuthorNotes: I am this person. When doing escape rooms I like to share my cognitive process out loud. Not for any other reason than it is a relic of my day job where sharing information to a team is vital to solving puzzles. So, here I am, poking a little fun at myself.

comics.Title: Role Playing Worlds
comics.AuthorNotes: I have seen many worlds. There are chill worlds, comfy, liminal, horror, clubs, bars, etc... but one such category I find the most fascinating are the role play worlds. They never advertise their subgenre in a way. It seems so unsuspecting. A McDonald's, a Starbucks. What impresses me the most, is that while not explicitly stated, people tend to get into 'character' so much. My favorite of this drama still remains the VRChat Drama Courts. People take being serious in virtual worlds very seriously.

comics.Title: Lollipop Toggles
comics.AuthorNotes: Ah yes, we have all been here. Newcomers to VRChat unsuspecting of the goon lords traps that liter the lands, try on what seems like an innocent toggle. A lollipop!??! Everytime a lollipop gets toggled, some newcomer loses their innocence.

comics.Title: Phantom Wall
comics.AuthorNotes: So many times in Full Body Tracking where you smash into a wall of your place and can't help but launch what it must look like to those watching you in VR Space hit a physical reality wall.

comics.Title: Patient Zero
comics.AuthorNotes: This is the beginning of the second story arc of the Imposters. Although I have left the Collector arc unfinished, I am still in the mode of building lore and canon for which to tell stories through. I chose the zombie apocalypse metaphor because I have been out and about at rave pop ups and would hear audibly the gasps, moans, and cries of everyone being pixelated as the event fills up. It was very much a moment when looking around and it seemed very Zombie-esque. The idea of having these pixelated zombies just fill the backdrop of a zone, just somewhat being there, but not fully engaged in the human aspect of connecting seemed appropriate.

comics.Title: Infection Spreads
comics.AuthorNotes: The Imposter storyline continues following the usual tropes of a zombie outbreak movie. First comes Patient Zero, the scientist who was ignored giving out the warning signs, to the initial 'spread' scene. This is how I imagine it went down for some of the Maximus factions.

comics.Title: Imposters
comics.AuthorNotes: One of my favorite video games was Max Payne. I still remember that noire style, cynical,  crude and cheesy 1 liners. I tried to mimic that style here as a nameless narrator during the events of the spread describe the rave worlds. In a zombie movie analogy, this is the part of the movie where the characters finally realize the scale and scope of world events. It is also of interest here to name the 'mob' villain.

comics.Title: Safe Haven
comics.AuthorNotes: Every zombie lore always has that 'safe haven'. The promise of safety where the price tag is generally freedom, free will, and submission. In such a bleak world with an overwhelming force of evil, it is easy to see the allure to people. It also generally implies someone mantains the order, or has an agenda thereof. What exactly? We shall see...

comics.Title: Wrong Reflection
comics.AuthorNotes: The setting is set. The factions, events, and general timeline has been introduced and established now. Now begins the micro moments of the people in these events. Here, we cut back to Patch. The Collector arc hasn't been finished yet, but I feel like these stories of Patch can be told in parallel. The characters must remain true to themselves so here you see Patch's innocence and 'heart of gold' and reinforces his philosophy that identity is something built, not merely worn. The thing that makes hero stories so great is that they have a weakness that is exploited and generally speaking, is the weakness used to defeat the adversary after a catharsis moment and of losing all hope in setbacks. Here, we see how Patch would have handled during the spread and Imposter outbreak and it seen with Patch, well... patching  victims and helping.

comics.Title: Last Call
comics.AuthorNotes: One of this arcs main characters is introduced here as he recalls the events of the Spread's beginning. Due to his background in the crasher gangs of the Velvet Rope Club wars and former winner of the Velvet Trials, we see their background is particurlary adept at surviving. Survival comes at a cost. This also introduces the lore and canon of one of my favorite parody zones: The Trashed Trophy Tavern, a world where people go to talk about how trashed they are, how trashed they can get, how trashed they are getting, and how early since waking up they get trashed.

comics.Title: Last Stand
comics.AuthorNotes: The story transitions from the events known as 'Last Call' to the save haven location of 'Last Stand' and shows the change of character, the loss it was spurred by, and the moral code of the Last Stand colony. Unlike Patch who has the moral propensity to try and save, the crasher here is again, pitted at the opposing ideal. He is cold and calculating... but gets results and is one to strike pre-emptively. Again, I really enjoyed keeping to that noire overt metaphor motiff

comics.Title: The Last Public Instance
comics.AuthorNotes: A classic zombie style conflict. A group refuses to lock their world to the public but this means opening themselves to danger. Their leader says public instances are the whole reason VRChat exists and they will not become another gated fortress. There is social commentary here on the nature of VRChat and the worlds therein. Refugees continue arriving and so do other things. The purpose of this scene is to create a polar opposite of the Last Stand colony who believes in authoritarian lockdowns. A debate that mimics the physical world's events of the past decade, with themes that should be familiar to draw your own personal parallels to. The typical tropes of taking on survivors vrs. risk as told through the Maximus canon along with its accompanying themes: such as turning into the dangers you claim to stand against and the willingness to help strangers, and the importance of keeping your humanity.

comics.Title: The Morning After
comics.AuthorNotes: The last public instance is still standing, but the threat of the worlds can not be ignored for much longer. Fights are still breaking out and an uWu embassy diplomat tries to keep the peace in dealing with the differences of the survival groups until an avatar fully converts to an Imposter. The evidence of seeing it shatters the remaining denialism.

comics.Title: Cost of Staying Open
comics.AuthorNotes: The opposing sides keep going back and forth as the camp is beginning to turn.

Patch shows up with other refugees at the Last Public Instance. His custom avatar patching renders him immune to the Imposters but also immune to scanning. The origins and nature of patch's avatar are unique. While in the updated security screen another Imposter is converted. Patch begins noticing a pattern to the outbreak and demonstrates through a form of self destruction the willingness to pay a cost for a greater good.

The idea of non optimized avatars as being one of the causes to a zombification of VR avatars seem ironically appropriate considering the vanity and typical anti-materialism themes it connotes. Patch shows his analytical, more methodological ways over the emotional hard stances of the crowds bumper sticker like dogma. I also grin at the idea that the hats are the one prop society as a whole was willing to part ways with. After all, now they can see their wonderful avatar hairs at the Crystal Mirror Den. Actually, my archtype imagery of a mirror world is this Frozen Elsa like ice castle made of crystals and mirror like reflections. Very shard like. I don't know if Crystal Mirror Den is the best name but I am sure there will be another one should its world arise. A bit of an easter egg in a ways, when I do montage scene cuts on the panels, I like to pick potential new areas. The strip of the two adventurers, one being mute and saying ... for hours to reveal the lol at the end. In that strip they step into the Crystal Mirror world as one of the adventures going by while still seeing the ...
